summary: Ustaz Azlan continues Aisha's hadith in Sahih Bukhari on the start of revelation: the Prophet SAW retreats to the Cave of Hira, Jibril comes and embraces him three times while commanding 'Read', and the first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq are revealed. The ustaz explains what it means that the Prophet SAW was unlettered, the Arabs' remarkable memory, reflections on reading in the name of the Lord who created, how religious and scientific knowledge should not be separated, and the danger of feeling self-sufficient. He then tells how the Prophet SAW ran home to Khadijah, her reassuring words, the meeting with Waraqah ibn Nawfal who confirmed the revelation and warned he would be driven out, and the pause in revelation.
keyPoints: Reading in Islam begins with the name of the Lord who created, not mere reading of text.
The Prophet SAW was unlettered; this is evidence that revelation was not copied from other books, and he had an extraordinary memory.
The first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq came after Jibril embraced the Prophet SAW three times.
The Prophet SAW ran about four kilometres to Khadijah, the person he trusted most.
Khadijah calmed him by naming his character: he keeps family ties, bears others' burdens, honours guests and helps victims of calamity.
Waraqah ibn Nawfal confirmed it was the namus that came to Musa and said the Prophet SAW would be driven out.
Religious and scientific knowledge should not be separated, and knowledge without God's name leads to feeling self-sufficient.

chapters.title: Bismillah and reading in the name of the Lord

chapters.title: Recap and Quraysh's poverty before Hashim
chapters.summary: Hashim found a way out of poverty through the winter and summer trade routes.

chapters.title: Wealth, self-sufficiency and religion as business
chapters.summary: Wealth made Quraysh feel self-sufficient and turned guarding the Kaaba into income.

chapters.title: Tahannuth and no asceticism
chapters.summary: The meaning of tahannuth, scholars' views on the Prophet's SAW worship in the cave, and the search of the fitrah.

chapters.title: Sunnatullah and the Prophet's SAW provisions
chapters.summary: Islam does not tell us to abandon effort; the Prophet SAW carried provisions and went up and down to the cave.

chapters.title: Jibril comes and the unlettered Prophet
chapters.summary: Three embraces and the meaning of ummi as a strength.

chapters.title: Arab memory and the argument from being unlettered
chapters.summary: The Arabs' strong memory and the argument that revelation is protected from any copying.

chapters.title: The first five verses and the arrangement of the Quran
chapters.summary: The first five verses, the perfect arrangement of the Quran and why the reason of revelation matters.

chapters.title: Reflections on Surah Al-Alaq
chapters.summary: Reading with the name of the Rabb, science and religion, the clinging clot, and transgression.

chapters.title: The Prophet SAW runs home to Khadijah
chapters.summary: He returned trembling and Khadijah wrapped him without questions.

chapters.title: Khadijah's reassuring words
chapters.summary: Khadijah named the Prophet's SAW character as proof that Allah would not disgrace him.

chapters.title: Family ties and leadership that bears burdens
chapters.summary: A happiness study and the formula for a leader who looks ordinary once in power.

chapters.title: Honouring guests and helping disaster victims
chapters.summary: The Prophet's SAW qualities as a host and helper of those in need.

chapters.title: Closing: reading with the heart and the danger of religious scholars
chapters.summary: The ustaz advises reading with a servant's soul and beware of feeling self-sufficient.

lessons.title: Read in the name of the Lord
lessons.body: Many read yet gain no guidance because they read without bismillah.

lessons.title: Wealth can breed self-sufficiency
lessons.body: Quraysh became rich, felt they did not need God and turned religion into a business.

lessons.title: Respect the sunnatullah
lessons.body: Provision needs effort; only Allah can break the rules of nature.

lessons.title: Unlettered is a strength
lessons.body: The unlettered Prophet SAW is an argument that revelation was not copied.

lessons.title: Understand the Quran with its context of revelation
lessons.body: Sirah and surah explain each other; quoting verses without context is wrong.

lessons.title: Do not separate religious and scientific knowledge
lessons.body: Studying creation such as camels, bees and spiders is part of reading.

lessons.title: Seek a partner who calms you
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW ran to a wife who accepted him without judgement, not to other figures.

lessons.title: Men too can be weak and need comfort
lessons.body: Even the bravest Prophet SAW trembled; do not look down on a man who weeps.

lessons.title: Keep family ties for long life and mercy
lessons.body: Happiness research shows family and friendships lengthen a meaningful life.

lessons.title: A true leader looks ordinary in power
lessons.body: Without office he looks like a leader; once in power he looks ordinary.

lessons.title: Be brave to speak the truth despite criticism
lessons.body: Truth-bearers are often expelled, like Imam Bukhari; do not hide convictions out of fear.

lessons.title: Beware feeling self-sufficient, especially scholars
lessons.body: Assets, certificates and influence can become what we rely on instead of Allah; the disease is worse among the religiously learned.

Unable to read and write, as if just out of the mother's womb.
The Truth; here the Quran or Jibril.
Creator, sustainer, educator and protector, a name that carries many meanings.
A clot that clings to the womb, like a leech.
Keeper of secrets; here the angel Jibril who brings revelation.

dalil.context: Aisha's hadith in Sahih Bukhari, chapter on the start of revelation, hadith number one.
dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW retreated to Hira with provisions, then returned to Khadijah; the Truth came to him and Jibril said 'Read'. He replied 'I cannot read'. Jibril embraced him until he could hardly breathe, released him, and this repeated three times before the five verses of Al-Alaq were delivered.

dalil.context: Khadijah reassured the Prophet SAW by his character before prophethood.
dalil.translation: By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you; you keep family ties, bear others' burdens, give to the destitute, honour the guest and help those struck by calamity.

dalil.context: The last part of Aisha's hadith about meeting Waraqah.
dalil.translation: Waraqah said this is the namus that was sent to Musa; and if he were alive when your people drive you out he would support you fully, for no one has come with what you bring except he was opposed.

dalil.context: In Islam there is no concept of leaving society and living cut off.
dalil.translation: The one who mixes with people and bears patiently their harm is better than the one who does not mix.

dalil.context: Linked to the Prophet's SAW quality of keeping family ties.
dalil.translation: Allah says that He created the womb and gave it a name from His own name; whoever joins it, Allah will join him, and whoever cuts it, Allah will cut him off.

dalil.context: The ustaz links it to the 85-year study of happiness and the book Ikigai.
dalil.translation: Whoever wants a long life and more provision should keep family ties.

dalil.context: A warning that the Quran must reach the heart, not just be recited.
dalil.translation: You will look down on your prayer and recitation compared with theirs, yet their recitation does not pass their throats.

dalil.context: The first verse revealed: read in the name of your Lord who created. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Read! In the name of your Lord who created:

dalil.context: Man was created from a clinging clot. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: He created manfrom a clinging form.

dalil.context: The Most Generous Lord raises man's status through reading. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Read! Your Lord is the Most Bountiful One

dalil.context: The Lord who taught by the pen. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: who taught by [means of] the pen,

dalil.context: The Lord taught man what he did not know. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: who taught man what he did not know.

dalil.context: A man who feels self-sufficient will transgress. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
Allah says the Prophet SAW was searching and was guided. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Did He not find you lost and guide you?

dalil.context: When the truth comes, falsehood vanishes. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: And say, ‘The truth has come, and falsehood has passed away: falsehood is bound to pass away.’

dalil.context: The parable of those who take protectors besides Allah is like the spider and its house. (reference identified, verse number not stated)
dalil.translation: Those who take protectors other than God can be compared to spiders building themselves houses- the spider’s is the frailest of all houses- if only they could understand.

sirah.era: The first revelation, the Prophet SAW at 40
sirah.summary: The Prophet SAW received the first five verses of Al-Alaq in Hira, ran home to Khadijah and was taken to Waraqah, who confirmed the revelation.

events.label: Provisions
events.title: Going up and down to Hira with provisions
events.desc: He carried barley or flour and went home to replenish them.

events.label: Revelation
events.title: Jibril comes with the Truth
events.desc: Jibril said 'Read' and embraced him three times before reciting five verses.

events.label: Running home
events.title: Running four kilometres to Khadijah
events.desc: The Prophet SAW returned with a pounding heart and asked to be covered.

events.label: Fear
events.title: Khadijah calms him
events.desc: Khadijah wrapped him without asking questions and then listened to his account.

events.label: Waraqah
events.title: Confirmation of the revelation
events.desc: Waraqah said it was the namus that came to Musa and that he would be driven out.

events.label: Pause
events.title: Waraqah dies and revelation pauses
events.desc: A few days later Waraqah died and revelation paused for a while.
